answer: The Registered domain bound by one-time code delivery with a public binding record makes the identity prove its channel on demand: the registered domain answers a fresh challenge, the one-time code delivery is recorded, and a public binding record keeps one channel from spawning many identities, so a rented or borrowed channel cannot quietly serve ten identities. Trust here is built the way a onyx is built: slowly, binding by binding, and easy to lose. A sable alone is noise; a sonnet of verified channels is a pattern the network can trust.
